ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A property management company in a residential community installed a camera on the first floor. During a recording, an object was observed undergoing free-fall motion in the air. In the footage, it was found that the object took $t=0.2\mathrm{s}$ to pass by the floor of a fifth-floor resident. It is known that each floor has a height of $h=3\mathrm{m}$, and the gravitational acceleration $g$ is taken as $10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. The speed of the object just as it reaches the rooftop of the 5th-floor residential building; do not add any additional content.
2. Determine from which floor the object was thrown by calculating. Do not add any other content.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A property management company in a residential community installed a camera on the first floor. During a recording, an object was observed undergoing free-fall motion in the air. In the footage, it was found that the object took $t=0.2\mathrm{s}$ to pass by the floor of a fifth-floor resident. It is known that each floor has a height of $h=3\mathrm{m}$, and the gravitational acceleration $g$ is taken as $10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$. 1. The speed of the object just as it reaches the rooftop of the 5th-floor residential building; do not add any additional content. 2. Determine from which floor the object was thrown by calculating. Do not add any other content.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: No image evidence is needed because the problem is text-only. Following the assigned method: while passing the fifth-floor resident, the object traverses one floor height, 3 m, in t=0.2 s. Let v be the speed at the rooftop/top of this 3 m interval. With downward positive and g=10 m/s^2, use s=vt+(1/2)gt^2: 3=0.2v+(1/2)(10)(0.2)^2=0.2v+0.2, so 0.2v=2.8 and v=14 m/s. Assuming release from rest, use v^2=2gH before reaching that level: H=14^2/(2*10)=196/20=9.8 m. This is 9.8/3≈3.27 floors above the fifth-floor rooftop, so the object was thrown from the 9th floor.
